text.p: Israel's Elite Industries Ltd announced on Thursday that the Federman group had put in motion a mechanism to dissolve shared control of the company with Gideon Holdings.

"The Federman group informed Gideon Holdings, which is controlled by the Strauss family, of its desire to acquire all the Strauss group's shares in the company," Elite told the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
The Strauss family holds at least 12.9 percent of equity and voting rights of 20 percent in Elite.
The company said the offer comes under a "Buy Me, Buy You" deal between the sides contained in an agreement signed at the time they established joint control of the company in February 1996.

Under the agreement, Strauss can accept the offer or declare within 60 days that it will acquire the Federman stake in Israel's largest publicly traded food manufacturer at a 2.5 percent discount to that offered by Federman, Elite said.

Federman has offered to pay 38 shekels ($11.28) for every Elite 1 ordinary share and 67.25 shekels for every par 5 ordinary share held by Gideon in Elite. Elite 5 shares closed at 82.46 shekels on Wednesday, up 3.25 percent.

Elite officials were not available to comment on Thursday's announcement but Israel's Globes business newspaper said the offer came after the two sides had decided to dissolve joint control of the company.
The newspaper said the partners were at loggerheads over managerial and strategic issues.

The Federman group has a 13 percent equity holding, which give its voting rights equal to 26.28 percent. Globes said the shares were collateral for loans of more than $20 million the family used to buy the holdings of the British commodities firm ED&F Man in Elite last year.
The family, which is led by David Federman, Elite's chairman, turned around shortly after buying the Man shares and sold 15 percent of Elite to the Strauss family.
Elite has undergone far-reaching changes since the Strauss family came on the scene. Much of the company's loss-making European businesses, acquired in 1992, have been closed or sold off.

Earlier on Thursday, Elite reported net earnings reached 18.42 million shekels in 1996, turning around from a 6.79 million loss. The company took a 20.5 million shekel charge for the year on reorganisations.

But equity analysts say the company faces an increasingly competitive domestic market, where many other food makers have forged strategic alliances with multinational companies. The Strauss family's principal holding, Strauss Dairies, has joint venture agreements with Unilever and Danone.
